learning_objective: 🎯 Discover the science of what you eat! Learn how a balanced diet fuels your body, prevents diseases, and keeps you fit during your growing years.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Food is what we eat; nutrition is how our body uses that food. Nutrients are the chemical substances in food that provide energy, build tissues, and regulate body processes.
A balanced diet contains all essential nutrients—carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, and water—in the correct proportions to meet the body's daily requirements.

Because adolescents are growing rapidly, they need more calories, protein, iron (especially for girls), and calcium (for bone mass) than adults. Skipping meals or relying on junk food causes deficiencies.

Health is a state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being. Fitness is the body's ability to perform daily tasks with energy. Both require good nutrition, regular exercise, and adequate sleep.
Obsession with body image can lead to dangerous disorders like Anorexia Nervosa (starving oneself due to fear of gaining weight) and Bulimia (binge eating followed by vomiting).

fun_activity.title: 🥗 Rainbow Plate Challenge
fun_activity.instructions: For dinner tonight, try to have at least 3 different natural colors on your plate (e.g., green spinach, orange carrots, white rice). Different colors usually mean a wider variety of vitamins and minerals!

exam_tips: 📌 Clearly define the difference between Macronutrients (needed in large amounts: carbs, proteins) and Micronutrients (needed in small amounts: vitamins, minerals).
📌 Understand why Calcium and Iron are critically important during adolescence.
📌 Be ready to write a short note on Anorexia Nervosa and Bulimia.
quick_recap: ⭐ A balanced diet is the foundation of good health and immunity.
⭐ Junk food is typically 'empty calories'—high in sugar/fat but low in real nutrients.
⭐ Physical fitness improves not just your body, but also your mental focus and mood.
